test_cases.description: Verify that render_individual with max_tokens=None returns output byte-identical to the pre-budget-cap implementation.
preconditions: A valid Spec object is constructed with all artifacts populated
test_cases.input: A Spec object with architecture, test_spec, and PRD; max_tokens=None
test_cases.expected: The returned dict is byte-identical to calling render_individual without the max_tokens parameter
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode:
spec = build_test_spec_with_all_artifacts()
result_with_none = render_individual(spec, max_tokens=None)
result_legacy = render_individual(spec)
assert result_with_none == result_legacy
for key in result_legacy:
    assert result_with_none[key] == result_legacy[key]

test_cases.description: Verify that render_individual applies progressive truncation when Level 0 exceeds the budget, returning the first level that fits or Level 2.
preconditions: A valid Spec object is constructed such that Level 0 render exceeds 300 estimated tokens
test_cases.input: A Spec with architecture and test_spec whose Level 0 render totals 500 tokens; max_tokens=300
test_cases.expected: Returned dict has estimated token sum ≤ 300 (Level 1 or Level 2 applied), or is the Level 2 render if neither fits
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode:
spec = build_spec_with_large_content(level0_tokens=500)
result = render_individual(spec, max_tokens=300)
total = sum(estimate_tokens(v) for v in result.values())
assert total <= 300 or result == render_individual_at_level2(spec)
assert 'architecture' not in result  # Level 1 at minimum was applied

test_cases.description: Verify that render_individual returns the Level 0 render without truncation when the budget is sufficient.
preconditions: A valid Spec object is constructed such that Level 0 render is ≤ 200 estimated tokens

test_cases.expected: Returned dict is identical to the Level 0 render; architecture key is present

result = render_individual(spec, max_tokens=200)
result_full = render_individual(spec, max_tokens=None)
assert result == result_full
assert 'architecture' in result

test_cases.description: Verify that budget evaluation sums estimate_tokens(v) for all values in the result dict, with empty strings contributing 0.
preconditions: A valid Spec object is constructed with at least one artifact producing an empty string value
test_cases.input: A Spec where one artifact value is an empty string and others have content
test_cases.expected: Budget evaluation counts the empty-string artifact as 0 tokens; total equals sum of non-empty values only
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode:
spec = build_spec_with_empty_artifact()
result = render_individual(spec, max_tokens=None)
total = sum(estimate_tokens(v) for v in result.values())
assert estimate_tokens('') == 0
assert total == sum(estimate_tokens(v) for v in result.values() if v != '')

test_cases.description: Verify that Python and Go produce structurally equivalent output (same keys present/absent, same truncation level) for the same spec and max_tokens.
preconditions: The same Spec is loadable in both Python and Go implementations
Both implementations are at the same version

test_cases.expected: Both outputs have the same set of keys present and the same truncation level applied
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode:
spec_py = load_spec_python(spec_path)
spec_go = load_spec_go(spec_path)
N = 300
result_py = render_individual(spec_py, max_tokens=N)

assert set(result_py.keys()) == set(result_go.keys())
assert truncation_level(result_py) == truncation_level(result_go)

test_cases.description: Verify that Python estimate_tokens and Go EstimateTokens return the same integer for any string input.
preconditions: Both Python and Go implementations are available
test_cases.input: A set of test strings of varying lengths
test_cases.expected: Both functions return the same integer for each string
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode:
for text in ['', 'a', 'abcd', 'abcdefghijklmnop', 'x' * 1000]:
    py_result = estimate_tokens(text)
    go_result = EstimateTokens(text)
    assert py_result == go_result == len(text) // 4

property_tests.description: For any string of any length, estimate_tokens must return exactly len(text) // 4.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random strings of length 0 to 10000 using hypothesis.strategies.text(min_size=0, max_size=10000) for Python; use random byte sequences converted to string for Go
property_tests.invariant_check: assert estimate_tokens(text) == len(text) // 4 for Python; assert EstimateTokens(text) == len(text) / 4 (integer division) for Go

property_tests.description: For any Spec value, rendering with max_tokens=None must produce byte-identical output to the legacy (no-argument) render.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate Spec objects with varying combinations of artifacts (architecture present/absent, test_spec present/absent, varying PRD body lengths) using hypothesis composite strategies or Go fuzzing
property_tests.invariant_check: assert render_individual(spec, max_tokens=None) == render_individual(spec) for Python; assert reflect.DeepEqual(spec.RenderIndividual(), spec.RenderIndividual()) for Go (no options vs no options)

property_tests.description: For any Spec and any positive integer M, the budget-capped render either fits within M tokens or is the Level 2 render (no further truncation possible).
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate Spec objects with varying content sizes and positive integers M from 1 to 10000 using hypothesis.strategies.integers(min_value=1, max_value=10000) combined with Spec generation strategies
property_tests.invariant_check: result = render_individual(spec, max_tokens=M); total = sum(estimate_tokens(v) for v in result.values()); assert total <= M or result == render_individual_level2(spec)

property_tests.description: For any Spec with an architecture section, Level 1 truncation always removes the architecture key from the result dict.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate Spec objects that have a non-empty architecture section with varying content sizes using hypothesis composite strategies
property_tests.invariant_check: result = render_individual(spec, max_tokens=M_triggering_level1); assert 'architecture' not in result

property_tests.description: For any TestSpec with at least one test case, the slim render omits assertion_pseudocode, input, and expected content from all entries.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate TestSpec objects with 1 to 20 test cases containing random assertion_pseudocode, input, and expected values using hypothesis composite strategies
property_tests.invariant_check: result = _render_test_spec_slim(ts); for each test case tc in ts: assert tc.assertion_pseudocode not in result (when non-empty); assert tc.input not in result (when non-empty and sufficiently unique); assert tc.expected not in result (when non-empty and sufficiently unique)

property_tests.description: For any Spec and any positive integer N, Python and Go produce dicts with the same set of keys and the same truncation level.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate Spec objects loadable in both Python and Go with varying content sizes, and positive integers N from 1 to 5000; serialize the spec to a shared format and load in both implementations
property_tests.invariant_check: result_py = render_individual(spec_py, max_tokens=N); result_go = RenderIndividual(spec_go, WithMaxTokens(N)); assert set(result_py.keys()) == set(result_go.keys()); assert truncation_level_of(result_py) == truncation_level_of(result_go)

property_tests.description: For any Spec and any max_tokens value, the PRD body content is always present in the rendered output at every truncation level.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate Spec objects with non-empty PRD bodies and max_tokens values from None/0 to very small positive integers using hypothesis strategies
property_tests.invariant_check: for max_tokens in [None, 0, 1, 100, 10000]: result = render_individual(spec, max_tokens=max_tokens); assert spec.prd_body in concatenated_values(result); result_combined = render_combined(spec, max_tokens=max_tokens); assert spec.prd_body in result_combined

property_tests.description: For any Spec, max_tokens=0 and max_tokens=None produce identical output across all three render functions.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate Spec objects with varying combinations of artifacts using hypothesis composite strategies
property_tests.invariant_check: assert render_individual(spec, max_tokens=0) == render_individual(spec, max_tokens=None); assert render_individual_scoped(spec, 1, max_tokens=0) == render_individual_scoped(spec, 1, max_tokens=None); assert render_combined(spec, max_tokens=0) == render_combined(spec, max_tokens=None)

property_tests.description: For any Spec and any positive max_tokens, the progressive truncation evaluation loop terminates in at most 3 iterations (Level 0, Level 1, Level 2) — no unbounded looping.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate Spec objects with varying content sizes and positive max_tokens values from 1 to 100000 using hypothesis strategies
property_tests.invariant_check: Instrument the evaluation loop to count iterations; result = render_individual(spec, max_tokens=M); assert loop_iteration_count <= 3
